article_content: The French Navy captured 11 pirates on Sunday after they reportedly misidentified the military vessel Nivose as a commercial ship. Capt. Christophe Prazuck stated that two pirate speedboats approached at high speed before a French helicopter deterred them with warning shots. The group, operating from a mothership 1,000 km east of Mombasa, Kenya, possessed AK-47 rifles and rocket-propelled grenades. This interception occurs during an EU anti-piracy mission near Somalia, where the Nivose has detained 24 suspects in three weeks. Over the past year, more than 100 pirates have been apprehended, with most transferred to France, Somalia, or Kenya per international agreements. Recent incidents include the hijacking of the Almezaan cargo ship near Somalia's Harradera coast and the seizure of the MV Ariana bulk carrier with 35,000 tons of soybeans northwest of Seychelles. NATO reports indicate pirates continue exploiting regional instability, with ransom demands escalating to millions.
translated_content: Angkatan Laut Prancis nangkep 11 bajak laut dina Minggu sawirénné salah ngenalin kapal perang Nivose dados kapal dagang. Kaptén Christophe Prazuck ngwéntenang dua speedboat bajak laut nggegirisi kapal nika, nanging helikopter Prancis masang tembakan peringatan. Grup niki makarya saking kapal induk 1.000 km sisi kangin Mombasa (Kenya), madué bedil AK-47 miwah granat roket. Kajadiané terjadi rikala operasi EU ngalawan bajak laut ring Somalia, dija Nivose suba tangkep 24 tersangka ring tiga minggu. Saking setaun liwat, lewih saking 100 bajak laut katangkep, akéhné kaadiliang di Prancis, Somalia, utawi Kenya miturut perjanjian internasional. Kajadian anyar ngambah perampokan kapal Almezaan sisi basis Harradera Somalia miwah kapal MV Ariana sane mabin kedelai 35.000 ton di barat laut Seychelles. NATO neduang bajak laut tiang ngeksploitasi situasi énggal-énggalan, antaran tebusan suba nganjak nganti yuta-yuta dolar.

article_content: Brighton manager Chris Hughton recognizes the Football Association's intensified efforts to boost racial diversity in coaching positions but insists measurable hiring results must accompany verbal pledges. With merely three black managers currently in the game - despite 25% of players coming from minority backgrounds - Hughton gears up for Sunday's FA Cup Fourth Round match against Arsenal. The seasoned coach highlighted growing enrollment of BAME (Black, Asian, and Minority Ethnic) candidates in coaching courses as progress, while urging clubs to implement fair interview processes and clear feedback systems. Though understanding the intent behind the NFL's Rooney Rule, which requires interviewing minority candidates, Hughton favors voluntary industry action over mandated quotas. 'Real change,' he asserted, 'springs from authentic commitment, not just rule compliance.' Reflecting on his trailblazing career, Hughton added: 'Representation matters. If my journey motivates others, that's the greatest reward.'
translated_content: Manajer Brighton Chris Hughton ngaketin upaya Football Association ngelimbangin keragaman rasial di posisi pelatih, tusing nyidang hasil nyata patut keto. Dijemak tiga keto manajer kulit ireng mangkin - yadiastun 25% pamain saking minoritas - Hughton nyiapang timné ngadep Arsenal dina Piala FA Minggu. Pelatih senior né ngandikang paningkatan peserta kursus BAME (Kulit Ireng, Asia, miwah Minoritas Étnis) dados progres, sakewala ngajak klub nglaksanayang proses wawancara adil tur sistem umpan balik jelas. Sané ngerti maksud 'Rooney Rule' NFL sané ngwajibang ngwawancara calon minoritas, Hughton luwih milih aksi sukarela saking kuota wajib. 'Parobahan nyata,' keto copotné, 'mawit saking komitmen tulus, tusing seken aturan.' Mirengang karir perintisné, Hughton nambahin: 'Perwakilan penting. Yén lelintihan tiang nyemangatin len, punika ganjaran pinih agung.'

article_content: A Sydney mother has vowed to boycott Gnome Café in Surry Hills after claiming staff asked her to leave because her 11-month-old son was in a pram. Jessica Smith, 35, stated her morning coffee outing turned humiliating when employees allegedly said there was insufficient space for the pram, despite the café being nearly empty. 'I found it unreasonable – if it were a bar, I'd understand,' the Redfern resident told Daily Mail Australia. Management clarified they welcome children but maintain space constraints for prams in the small venue. Smith noted she'd positioned the pram against a wall and observed few customers during her visit. The incident sparked social media backlash, with multiple parents calling the policy discriminatory. The café reiterated its space limitations while expressing regret for any inconvenience caused.
translated_content: Ibu saking Sydney janji ngeboikot Gnome Café di Surry Hills sasubané kena usir margine ada kréta bayi anakné sané 11 bulan. Jessica Smith, 35 tiban, nyritayang pengalamané ngerusak liu ri kala karyawan café ngomong tusing ada ruang ajak kréta, maski café sepi. 'Nyené jengah pesan – di bar patut tusing keto,' keto ia ring Daily Mail Australia. Pengurus café nepukin i rahina ngelah pang singgah anak anake, nanging ruangné cenik tusing nyukup ajak kréta. Smith negesang kréta suba di pojok tur pengunjung tusing akéh. Kejadian niki ngawinang protés di media sosial, akéh ibu sane nyebut kabijakan niki diskriminasi. Café nepak ajak alasan ruang cenik, sakéwala matur nyesel ri kala wentén sane kérasan.
